title: Meeting Archbishop Marcinkus at the Vatican Bank

tellings.quote: and I and I looked up and he said we know about you from your boyhood with a lot of our associates in the mafia.

plain: In 1973, at the Vatican Bank, Archbishop Marcinkus is said to have greeted a young American visitor by telling him the Church already knew about him from his boyhood, through "a lot of our associates in the mafia." That visitor was Harold Malmgren, a former adviser to US presidents, and he tells Michels about the meeting himself, naming Pete Peterson in connection with it. If it happened that way, it suggests the Vatican's bank kept track of people through ties to organised crime.
